sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 1.6 'Transcriptions of the Mpi language' (thesis pp. 12-28 = pp. 40-56) gives initials, vowels, six tones on monosyllables in isolation (after Harris in the 1976 dictionary), tone sandhi, final consonants and voice quality, enclitics and pronoun inflection; no mention of stress or accent. Secs. 3.1.5 and 6.7 'Prominence' (thesis pp. 82, 129-130) describe phrase-level emphasis by 'a high pitch or a loud voice on that element' or by particles, not word stress. The abstract explicitly defers phonology to further study.

sources.note: An areal survey of tone/phonation/duration 'accents' in SE Asia; in sec. 3 'Morphophonemics' Benedict states that Mpi has six tones, all from splits of the three Proto-Burmese-Yipho tones, the three 'verbal tones' carrying an extra contour feature attributed to absorbed verbal/adjectival enclitics (i.e. the noun-tone vs verb-tone split reported by Matisoff 1978). Secondhand but explicit; agrees with the six-tone count of Harris/Srinuan 1976, Ladefoged & Maddieson 1996 and the 2009 TRF report, and not with Bradley 1977's 'identical to Akha' remark.
